title: Second Kummer cohomology of a curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a curve over algebraically closed $k$ in the sense of
[def-sc-curves]. It may be singular, non-reduced, disconnected or
have zero-dimensional components. Let $n>0$ be invertible in $k$.
Then

$$
H^2(C,\mu_n)\simeq\operatorname{Pic}(C)/n,
$$

where $\mu_n$, the Picard group, and cohomology are as in
[def-sc-kummer-sequence], [def-sc-picard-group], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].
The isomorphism is induced by the coboundary of the Kummer sequence,
$\operatorname{Pic}(C)=H^1(C,\mathbf G_m)\to H^2(C,\mu_n)$
([lem-sc-h1-gm-pic]). In particular $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0$
for every such $C$ ([lem-sc-brauer-zero-all-curves]).

proof.text: Since $C$ is a curve over algebraically closed $k$, [lem-sc-brauer-zero-all-curves] gives $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0$. The hypothesis that $n>0$ is invertible in $k$ makes $n$ invertible on $C$; [lem-sc-kummer-exact] says that the Kummer sequence of [def-sc-kummer-sequence] is then a short exact sequence of etale abelian sheaves $0\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{t\mapsto t^n}\mathbf G_m\to0$.

source.place: Tag 03PK, Lemma 59.28.1; Tag 03RQ, Lemma 59.69.1, Kummer-sequence argument

proof.text: Apply clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] to the short exact sequence from step 1, taking $X=Y=C$ and $u=\mathrm{id}_C$. Its degree-one and degree-two portion is $H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{H^1(t\mapsto t^n)}H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}H^2(C_{\Et},\mu_n)\to H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)$. The last group is zero by [lem-sc-brauer-zero-all-curves]. Under the group isomorphism of [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic], $H^1(t\mapsto t^n)$ is multiplication by $n$: the power map on the abelian sheaf $\mathbf G_m$ is the sum of $n$ identity maps, so its induced map on $H^1$ is multiplication by $n$, which the group isomorphism carries to multiplication by $n$ on $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$. Exactness gives $\ker\delta^1=n\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ and $\operatorname{im}\delta^1=H^2(C_{\Et},\mu_n)$. Thus the Kummer connecting map itself induces $\operatorname{Pic}(C)/n\operatorname{Pic}(C)\simeq H^2(C_{\Et},\mu_n)$; invert this isomorphism for the displayed orientation.
